input: Build a wooden raised bed for herbs

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The size and number of raised beds determines the amount of wood, soil, and hardware needed, and how complex the build will be.
Whether the bed is going on a patio, lawn, balcony, or ground affects the base design, drainage requirements, and anchoring method.
The available budget affects what type of wood can be used (e.g. cedar vs. treated pine) and whether purchased or reclaimed materials are viable.
Knowing if this is a solo DIY build or involves helpers, or whether the user is a beginner or experienced woodworker, shapes how detailed the instructions need to be.
Wood type and finish preferences (e.g. natural cedar, painted, stained) affect both aesthetics and the longevity/safety of the bed for edible herbs.
The tools already available to the user determine whether the plan requires cutting services, basic hand tools, or power tools, and affects the step-by-step approach.
Understanding whether the priority is quick assembly, long-term durability, visual appearance, or cost-efficiency helps rank the trade-offs in the plan.

gold.taskTitle: Build a wooden raised bed for herbs
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to construct a wooden raised garden bed specifically for growing herbs.

questions.title: What dimensions do you want the raised bed to be?
questions.description: Clarifies the target length, width, and height of the raised bed, which drives all material quantities.

questions.title: Where exactly will the raised bed be placed?
questions.description: Identifies the surface and setting — ground, patio, balcony, gravel, grass — which affects drainage and base design.

questions.title: What is your budget for this build?
questions.description: Determines the tier of wood and hardware that can realistically be used.

questions.title: How experienced are you with DIY woodworking projects?
questions.description: Calibrates the complexity of instructions and whether simpler joinery or beginner-friendly methods should be recommended.

questions.title: Do you have a preference for a specific type of wood?
questions.description: Establishes whether the user leans toward naturally rot-resistant options like cedar, or is open to treated pine or reclaimed timber.

questions.title: What tools do you currently have access to?
questions.description: Determines whether the plan should rely on hand tools, power tools, or pre-cut lumber from a supplier.

questions.title: What matters most to you — durability, looks, or low cost?
questions.description: Identifies the user's top priority so the plan can make the right trade-offs between longevity, aesthetics, and budget.
